gen-fs-nippo-gf-hedvig-letters-sans: Hedvig Letters Sans has a friendly, wide-mouthed look, with small letters that stand nearly as tall as capitals. Nippo is the sharper one, its curves holding firm at the shoulders, while Hedvig Letters Sans stays soft and low-key.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-heebo: Heebo is a plain sans with a tall central band of text and curves that stop short of closing. Heebo would look lost if Nippo shrank down, since Nippo's wire-cut, pressure-free line is made to stand out.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-hind-guntur: Hind Guntur draws tall lowercase like stamped metal type, with wide gaps where its curves meet the stems and no thick-thin shift at all. Nippo is the one for attention; Hind Guntur does the quiet work.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-hind-madurai: Tall, wide-open and a bit stamped-out, this pairing puts Nippo's wire-cut letters above Hind Madurai's lowercase, which fills the line almost like capitals. Both stand proud of the line, and that shared height is its strongest quality.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-hind-mysuru: Hind Mysuru is a plain sans with lowercase tops pressed close to the ascender line. Nippo adds a wiry, technical edge above it, while Hind Mysuru's open-mouthed a and unthinned strokes keep the text below steady.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-hind-siliguri: Hind Siliguri lays down a flat gray hum of constant line weight, its rounds gapped like a cracked bangle. Nippo, with its proud, wire-cut small letters, supplies the spark that this sans-serif keeps in reserve.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-hind-vadodara: Crisp, wiry and wide awake. Nippo's capital-sized small letters sit over Hind Vadodara, whose rounded glyphs have spacious gaps and tall bowls, so the sans-serif text feels open beneath the sharper heading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-huninn: Huninn is a plain sans whose lowercase rises close to cap height, with s terminals held clear of the body. Huninn feels sturdy and friendly beside Nippo's technical, wire-cut lettering, a softer neighbor to a sharper one.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-inter-tight: Small letters standing nearly capital-sized, cut like wire, are what mark Nippo out at the top. Inter Tight follows with rope-like lines, short ascenders and curve tails held well back, giving the sans a compact, modern hush.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-julius-sans-one: Nippo brings proud, wire-cut small letters that nearly match its capitals. Julius Sans One goes further, with almost no gap between capital and lowercase height and wide stretches of blank space between its open-ended curves.
